claims.statement: The console's HTTP surface consists of Next.js App Router handlers under apps/console/src/app/api/** backed by src/core modules (registry, state, mcp/sync, processes, skills, skillsSh/find/remove, installJobs, prompts, plugins, issues, cache, activity, sessions, memory) and six runtime adapters in src/runtimes/, with clients consuming them as RSC payloads, JSON, or SSE.

Every route that mutates console state follows the file-first ordering: mutate, run side effects, saveState() to .agents/console/state.json (atomic tmp+rename), invalidateDashboardCache(), respond, and only then does the client reconcile its zustand store - the client store never leads the file.
All mutating routes call invalidateDashboardCache(), so the 5-second TTL dashboard micro-cache never serves stale post-mutation data.

Install-job SSE streams (GET /api/tools/job?jobId=, GET /api/skills-sh/install?jobId=) are readers over on-disk logs .agents/console/tool-jobs/<id>.log plus status <id>.json, which makes them invariant to dev-mode HMR and route-bundle boundaries where an in-memory job Map would read empty.
The POST /api/tools/job/input and POST /api/skills-sh/install/input routes forward client input into the running job's stdin to drive interactive installers.

GET /api/runtimes?window= returns a cached full status snapshot of all runtimes (5 s TTL plus dedup), PATCH /api/runtimes persists the default runtime (star) selector into state.json, and GET /api/runtimes/list returns a probe-free lightweight list that feeds the client store.

GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/mcp manage the MCP registry and run a full multi-target sync on every mutation: PATCH accepts enabled (global toggle), runtimeOverride (per-runtime), or a wholesale transport replacement (stdio command/args/env, http url plus headers) without touching other fields; DELETE removes the server from exactly the target files the console previously wrote, via managed-name semantics that never touch foreign entries.

GET /api/mcp/catalog serves the MCP_PRESETS catalog (Context7, DeepWiki, WebMCP, Playwright plus serena/qmd/codegraph tool presets) and adapts stdio presets to the selected package manager (bunx versus npx -y) without rewriting already-installed servers.

GET /api/skills returns runtime skills with effective toggle state resolved as runtimeOverrides then defaults then useGlobal, and PATCH /api/skills persists toggles purely as overlays in state.json - skill files are never edited by the console.
GET /api/skills/installed lists installed harness skills (from .agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md, including skills.sh installs) together with their per-skill defaults.

POST /api/skills/create builds a creation prompt from the form (name, summary, details, examples) and spawns a new headless session on the skill-creation task runtime (or star default), placing the result in .agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md with the session appearing in the common session list.

POST /api/skills/remove runs bunx skills remove <name> -y (cleaning .agents/skills/<name>, the lock entry, and agent symlinks) with a coded manual fallback in core/skillRemove.ts that cleans the same locations if the CLI fails.

GET /api/skills-sh/search shells out to bunx skills find <query> as the primary path (the skills.sh HTTP API requires a Vercel OIDC token), parses ANSI-cleaned non-TTY output into owner/repo@skill install ids, caches results 60 s, and adds an HTTP fallback when fewer than 3 hits arrive.

GET /api/skills-sh/detail resolves a skill description through a cached 5-minute chain (registry snapshot under VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN, then og:description of the skill page, then GitHub repo page, then DeepWiki, then an iframe fallback) alongside a security audit from multiple trust providers, with all fetches subject to the SSRF allowlist.

POST /api/skills-sh/install spawns bunx skills add <pkg> -y (DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1, cwd = repo root) as a job that installs into .agents/skills/<name>, creates symlinks into detected agent directories, and writes skills-lock.json, with output streamed to the UI over SSE and stdin forwarding supported.

The /api/plugins routes manage bundle plugins whose MCP contribution physically enters state.mcp.servers on enable and is removed on disable only if the transport was not user-edited; install resolves the plugin {plugin:{id}} by id from trusted catalogs (builtin plus registered marketplaces) so arbitrary client-supplied plugin definitions are never accepted.

POST and DELETE /api/plugins/marketplace register and remove marketplace catalogs (validated name/URL, no duplicates); GET /api/plugins fetches catalog manifests through the SSRF filter - http/https only, localhost and private/reserved ranges banned, 10 s timeout, 512 KB response cap.
The only builtin plugin, chrome-devtools (MCP server chrome-devtools = npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest), lives in BUILTIN_PLUGINS in core/plugins.ts and installs from the Plugins tab in one click.

GET /api/processes?runtime= lists a runtime's processes from a single shared ps snapshot (TTL 2 s) filtered by the adapter's processPattern and classified app vs cli; POST /api/processes/action implements stop (SIGTERM, up to 3 s grace, then SIGKILL, with the PID re-verified against a fresh ps slice to guard against PID reuse) and restart (app-only via open -a; CLI processes cannot be restarted).

GET /api/sessions?runtime=&dir= lists session history per runtime filtered by console workspace dirs from per-runtime sources (claude/codex/zcode jsonl rollouts, kimi session_index.jsonl plus state.json); adding &id= returns metadata plus a text preview of the first ~30 transcript records while full data stays in the session file; opencode/cursor SQLite stores are unread and marked unsupported in the UI.

POST /api/sessions/reply answers a waiting session via a separate detached headless resume process (cwd = session dir, 120 s timeout) using per-runtime literal commands (claude -p --resume, codex exec resume, zcode via node zcode.cjs -p --resume, kimi --session -p, opencode run -s); cursor has no headless CLI and is not offered, and the user's interactive session is never touched.

POST /api/prompts/run launches a new detached headless session with output in .agents/console/runs/<ts>-<runtime>.log (gitignored), resolving the runtime as explicit request runtime, then settings.taskRuntimes.promptExecution, then defaultRuntime (star); the diagnostics Fix button builds its prompt via buildFixPrompt and uses this same route.

GET/PUT /api/settings read and write per-task runtime assignments (promptExecution, skillCreation) in state.settings.taskRuntimes, accepting only runtimes known to the harness with null meaning default (= star), and the client store updates only after the file write.

GET /api/tools, despite being a read, rewrites .agents/console/tools.env for the tool.sh dispatcher and lazily lifts autostarted dashboard services with retries throttled to at most once per 30 s; its status matrix covers system CLI, per-runtime markers, MCP registry, and dashboard liveness via TCP probe.

PUT /api/tools {packageManager} persists the Bun/NPM choice in .agents/console/package-manager.json (a sibling of state.json also written by setup.sh), applied to global npm-tool installs and stdio MCP catalog presets.

POST /api/tools/action drives the tool lifecycle (install, uninstall, reinstall, toggle, init, reinit with a dryRun preview mode) where uninstall steps are optional and never break a reinstall chain, state records merge marker-detected external installs so nothing is lost, and installations run as SSE-streamed jobs.

POST /api/tools/diagnose runs ToolDef-derived checks (CLI, dependencies, per-runtime integrations, MCP registry, dashboard TCP liveness, RTK hooks) with ok/critical/info symbols and, on critical failures, builds a headless fix prompt sent through /api/prompts/run on the prompt-execution runtime.

POST /api/tools/dashboard starts or stops standalone dashboard instances as detached processes (serena start-mcp-server with --enable-web-dashboard true overriding the user's web_dashboard:false config; headroom proxy --port 8787) with pids in .agents/console/dashboards.json and logs in .agents/console/logs/<id>-dashboard.log; the autostart toggle writes state.tools.autostart and immediately lifts or stops the console-owned instance, while agent-session-owned live dashboards are detected but never stopped.

GET /api/tools/usage merges console events from tools-usage.json (capped at 1000) with external metric snapshots (rtk gain --format json --all, ~/.headroom/proxy_savings.json or headroom savings) taken at most once per 5 minutes via CLI and files only - the server never issues HTTP requests to local tool ports.

GET/PUT /api/workspaces manage exactly one mandatory workspace (default repo root; replaceable but not deletable) plus additional ones; PUT validates absolute existing paths (with tilde expansion via expandHome) with no duplicates, and keeps state.workspaces.openwiki and state.workspaces.graphify as strict subsets of the list, silently pruning removed or foreign paths.

GET /api/workspaces/clone lists projects already cloned under sources/, and POST /api/workspaces/clone runs git clone of an https URL into sources/<name> as a job with terminal output, guarded by an SSRF host filter (https-only, no localhost or private/reserved networks).

GET /api/memory/docs returns recursive markdown trees of all workspaces skipping hidden directories, node_modules and .git, capped at 500 files and depth 8, with auto-selection of README then AGENTS then first file for the GFM renderer.

GET /api/memory/openwiki reports per-folder wiki status (tree, .last-update.json, build status, CLI availability) and re-syncs/prunes published visualizer slugs; POST /api/memory/openwiki/build spawns a detached literal openwiki --init (when openwiki/index.md is absent) or --update in the folder, with pid/mode in openwiki/.console-build.json and output in openwiki/.console-build.log, polled every 4 s.

GET /api/memory/graphify reports per-folder graph status and counters (from graph.json with an 8 MB parse cap); POST /api/memory/graphify/build launches detached graphify extract . (first run; update . thereafter) with metadata/log under graphify-out/.console-build.*; POST /api/memory/graphify/graph publishes graphify-out/graph.html into apps/console/public/graphify/<sha256-slug12>/ for a same-origin iframe (building is local via tree-sitter, viewing needs internet for unpkg).

GET /api/memory/runtimes?runtime= lists memory files written by the runtimes themselves, grouped per workspace plus a Global group (claude project memory dirs plus ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; codex ~/.codex/memories/ minus its sqlite store; zcode/kimi/opencode have no readable file memory; cursor memory lives in SQLite), and ?runtime= restricts the listing to one runtime for the per-runtime memory tab.

GET /api/memory/file?path= reads a single file only through the checkReadPath allowlist (core/memory.ts): markdown inside workspaces, non-hidden files under <dir>/openwiki/ and runtime memory directories, single global files like ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md - enforced with realpath containment, a ban on hidden path components, and a 1 MB cap; arbitrary paths are refused.

POST /api/memory/openwiki/visualizer runs the literal command openwiki visualize openwiki --export <dir>/openwiki/.visualizer (fully local, no LLM) and publishes a fixed 5-file set (index.html, client.js, client-lib.js, styles.css, graph.json) into apps/console/public/visualizers/<slug>/ where slug is the sha256 of the workspace path (gitignored), so the wiki graph embeds via same-origin iframe with no dynamic routes carrying user paths.

GET /dashboard/* is an embed proxy that forwards /dashboard/* to the literal upstream http://127.0.0.1:8787/dashboard/* (GET-only, code-literal host/port, framing headers like x-frame-options stripped from responses) so the Headroom dashboard - which sets x-frame-options: DENY - can render in an iframe; Serena's :24282 dashboard sets no framing header and is embedded directly without the proxy.

Route write effects respect the repository guard policy: the console writes only into .agents/console/ and managed MCP configs, never edits skill files or .agents/runtime vendor configs, and .gitignore is synchronized so secrets and machine-local console state stay out of git.
